# 7.7M-protein search. Bitscore cutoffs (GA) are invariant. Enforced by A13.

column7: SOLE entry filter (v2 3.1/3.2). Admits all four at GA: RP4 97, R751 90, pKM101 99, R388 121. Measured failure rate over 7,436 VirB4+: 0% by construction
Scores HIGHER on IncP (RP4 114 vs 97). Not required; kept as a sensitivity check on the VirB4-negative remainder

THRESHOLD CORRECTED 2026-09-14: was 'E<=1e-5 AND aa>150'. That rule is WITHDRAWN -- see docs/virb5_evalue_threshold_invalid.md. Its stated rationale was that GA loses RP4 trbJ (17.7 bits) and R751 trbJ (22.2) while E-values rescue them (7.9e-07, 3.4e-08). Measured under the pipeline's own hmmsearch (job 25913366) the SAME proteins score 17.7 bits E=0.22 and 22.2 bits E=0.0093: BOTH FAIL E<=1e-5. The rescuing E-values came from a protein-vs-Pfam scan (N~30,134 models), not a model-vs-proteome search (N=1,099,911). The rule never rescued its own controls. It was also STRICTER than the GA it replaced -- E=1e-5 falls at ~31.7 bits vs GA 24.7 -- costing ~177 plasmids while documented as a loosening (GA 5,545 vs E-rule 5,368). Its recorded count of 5,424 reproduces from NEITHER rule; the 56-plasmid residual is unexplained and recorded as such. MEASURED AT GA AND aa>150 (job 25913461): 5,545 of 7,436 = 25.4% failure. RP4 and R751 are recovered instead by the DISJUNCTION with CONJScan T4SS_T_virB5, which scores them 105.6 and 122.3 -- see data/anchors/anchor_disjunction_v1_1.tsv. With that disjunction VirB5 failure is 7.5%. The aa>150 conjunct is RETAINED and must appear on BOTH arms. TIER: 7.5% sits between the core band (4.1-4.9%) and the peripheral band (13.2-20.9%); VirB5 is assigned NO binary tier label -- carry the failure rate itself.

BLIND-SPOT CLAIM RETRACTED -- see docs/virb7_blindspot_RETRACTED.md. The family EXISTS (PF20898 P-type, PF06986 F-type). The earlier "no Pfam family" reading was an artefact of the labelling step: Pyrodigal does not call the 48 aa ORF at U09868.1:7899..8045, so nothing was ever scanned as VirB7. Usable for annotation; NOT for slot bounding, because the CALLER often will not supply the protein. Confirmed at scale by the ladder: PF20898 hits 206/7,436 = 2.8%, and PF06986 174/7,436 = 2.3%. A 97% failure rate for a family that demonstrably EXISTS is a caller limit, not a model limit -- these are 48 aa ORFs
